The depth of primary tillage depends considerably on the thickness of the fertile soil layer and on the preceding crops; in particular, if the preceding crops were vegetables or late silage crops, ploughing is done without stubble breaking. After stubble predecessors (legumes, cereals, perennial grasses) the tillage system includes stubble breaking, the depth of which depends on the type of weed infestation. With many annual weeds, stubble breaking is done at 6–8 cm, and where couch grass is present two diskings at 10–12 cm are used. Ploughing for carrots is done at 22–25 cm and, according to some sources, even 28–30 cm.

Fertilizers for organic carrot growing. Organic fertilizers are applied to the preceding crops, because applying organic matter directly under carrots can reduce root marketability by increasing the development of lateral roots. The ideal complex solution for applying organic fertilizers directly under carrots is GREENODIN, applied depending on soil acidity: on neutral and acidic soils with pH < 6.0, GREENODIN GRAY organic fertilizer is applied at 25 g/m² (250 kg/ha); on soils with an alkaline reaction (pH > 7.5), GREENODIN BROWN is applied at 25 g/m² (250 kg/ha).
